review_scope.selection_rule: up to three source excerpts per entry
review_scope.review_basis: A phrase is rejected when the excerpts show ordinary prose, a sector label, or a truncated institution name rather than a distinctive organisation mention.

preservation_rules: Require the complete organisation name or an explicitly documented corporate suffix variant; never publish a prefix ending in a coordinating word such as 'and'.
Reject matches that end at a grammatical stopword or begin with a generic fragment when the source excerpt continues to a longer institution name.
Reject ordinary noun phrases, idioms, sector labels, job descriptions, and policy concepts even when a supplier has a matching legal name.
Keep a short form only when the reviewed source uses it as a clear proper-name reference in context and it is distinctive enough to avoid common-language matches.
For government departments, preserve complete historically named departments but require jurisdiction or a complete department title when the short form could refer to several agencies.
Treat punctuation and case variants as equivalent only after the phrase has passed the substantive-name check; punctuation normalization must not turn a sentence fragment into an alias.
When one candidate has both incidental and genuine mentions, reject the broad alias and retain a longer, source-supported form where available.
